factProposals.value: An operator-uploaded hospital-system export is treated as parsed CSV rows (csv.DictReader output), not raw file bytes, once it reaches the mapping layer -- source-system detection and metric mapping both operate on column headers and cell values.

Each hospital system (Epic, Cerner, etc.) is represented by one mapping module declaring a fixed contract (FINGERPRINT_COLUMNS, HOSPITAL_ID_COLUMN, MONTH_COLUMN, is_totals_row, compute_metrics); detect_format() matches by an exact column-fingerprint subset, never a partial or fuzzy match, so adding a new vendor means adding one module rather than changing the normalizer.

The standard monthly metric set produced across all source systems is cash_on_hand, ar_balance, denial_rate_pct, and open_positions -- one row per (hospital, month, metric), verified to be identical in name and value across two different vendor export layouts for the same underlying data.

Operator-uploaded export data is treated as the management company's private data, not public data like the CMS HCRIS tables -- the two new tables (export_conversions, hospital_monthly_metrics) have RLS enabled with zero policies, which fails closed by this project's own convention, rather than the public-read policy the CMS tables use.

The PHI guardrail built for STORY-010 (reject files with patient names, birth dates, or record numbers) applies to this ingestion path too, not only the path it was first built for -- every export is scanned before either new table is touched, and a PHI hit is raised as a distinct condition rather than represented as a normal conversion outcome.

decisions.statement: Built under .colaberry's STORY-011 definition (Convert Hospital System Exports to Standard Metrics, REQ-011, release r1) rather than .hospulse's STORY-011 (an unrelated cost-report-co-pilot story, REQ-015, release r4).
decisions.rationale: This is a third instance of a numbering collision between the portal's plan (.colaberry) and this repo's own local plan (.hospulse) already documented and resolved the same way for STORY-010 and STORY-003. .hospulse's own equivalent of REQ-011 is fulfilled by its STORY-008, which is also not started, so there is no existing local work this collides with.

decisions.statement: Idempotency is keyed on a SHA-256 hash of the raw export file's bytes (export_conversions.source_file_hash), not the filename, and hospital_monthly_metrics upserts on (provider_ccn, month, metric_name).
decisions.rationale: A re-uploaded file with a new name is still the same file and must not be reprocessed as new; a corrected file with the same name is a genuinely different file and must be. Content hashing distinguishes the two cases the filename alone cannot.
decisions.evidence: pipeline/export_normalizer.py#compute_file_hash, #run; verified live: identical content under a different filename returned the first run's outcome with no second export_conversions row

decisions.statement: Reused phi_guardrail.ingest_file_with_phi_gate() from STORY-010 rather than duplicating PHI detection, and let a PHI hit raise PhiRejectedError rather than becoming another ConversionOutcome.status value.
decisions.rationale: The gate function was already built for exactly this kind of reuse. Folding a PHI rejection into .status would let a caller that only branches on .status mistake a security rejection for a normal, retryable conversion outcome (needs_mapping/failed) -- keeping it a distinct raised condition prevents that by construction.
decisions.evidence: pipeline/export_normalizer.py#run; verified live: an Epic-shaped export with an added "Patient Name" column was rejected before either new table was touched, with a structured audit log line naming the column/category/reason but not the value

decisions.statement: Extracted load_env() out of hcris_import.py and early_warning.py into pipeline/env.py once export_normalizer.py needed the same function.
decisions.rationale: This project's own composition rule sets three duplicated occurrences as the threshold for lifting shared logic; this was the third file to need an identical implementation.
decisions.evidence: pipeline/env.py; pipeline/hcris_import.py, pipeline/early_warning.py (now import load_env instead of defining it)

limitations.statement: Only two source-system mappings exist (Epic, Cerner), and both column layouts are illustrative -- built without a real vendor export sample, since none was available. A real vendor's mapping module would need a real sample to build against, the same way hcris_import.py's worksheet citations were all confirmed against a real downloaded file before being written.
No operator-upload path exists yet (STORY-005, not started) -- export_normalizer.run() takes raw file bytes directly as a function argument. There is no upload UI or API endpoint that calls it yet.

Month parsing accepts only ISO-shaped values ("YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM"). A vendor export using a different date format (e.g. "MM/YYYY") correctly produces a 'failed' outcome rather than being silently misparsed, but is not automatically handled -- a new format would need an explicit addition to _MONTH_FORMATS.

demonstrationEvidence.ref: pipeline/test_export_normalizer.py (14 tests: two vendor formats reconciling to identical standard metrics, unknown format and a one-column-short fingerprint both correctly needs_mapping, totals-row dropping without corrupting source_row provenance, a malformed month and a missing per-row column both producing failed rather than a crash, denial rate left None rather than a fake 0%, file-hash determinism, CSV round-tripping, and the PHI audit log line being valid JSON that never carries the flagged value); full pipeline/ suite (76 tests) run clean with no regressions
